questions.q: What does "developer-controlled" mean for an unlocked package?
options: Only Salesforce Support can modify it
Its metadata isn't hidden or obfuscated, and components can often remain editable in the org after install
It can only be created by a certified Technical Architect
It requires a managed package namespace to exist first
questions.explain: Unlocked packages are developer-controlled: metadata stays visible rather than hidden, and depending on how the package is built, components can remain editable after installation.

questions.q: Which scenario is the best fit for an unlocked package, per this lesson?
options: An ISV distributing a commercial app on AppExchange to customers it will never directly support
A shared set of internal custom objects and Apex utilities used across a single company's multiple internal orgs
A one-off Apex class that will never be deployed anywhere else
A scratch org definition file
questions.explain: Unlocked packages fit internal, cross-org application metadata within a single company well, since hiding implementation details from your own teams (the point of a managed package) would be counterproductive there.

questions.q: What does `sf package create --name "Shared Utilities" --package-type Unlocked --path force-app` do?
options: Installs a package into a target org
Registers a new unlocked package tied to the Dev Hub and a specific path in the project
Creates a new scratch org named Shared Utilities
Deletes an existing package permanently
questions.explain: sf package create registers a new package definition (here, type Unlocked) associated with the Dev Hub and tied to a given project path, recording it in sfdx-project.json's packageAliases.

questions.q: Why isn't a package definition alone installable — what has to exist first?
options: A package version, an immutable installable snapshot of the package's contents, created with sf package version create
A namespace must be registered first, even for unlocked packages
The Dev Hub must be disabled first
The package must be converted to managed type first
questions.explain: A package definition just registers the package; you need a package version — an immutable, installable snapshot created via sf package version create — before anything can actually be installed into a target org.

questions.q: What does the --installation-key-bypass flag do when creating a package version?
options: It bypasses the Dev Hub authentication requirement
It skips requiring an installation key (a password-like protection), common for internal packages not trying to prevent unauthorized installs
It automatically promotes the version to released
It deletes the installation key from all previous versions
questions.explain: --installation-key-bypass skips the installation key requirement — a protection mechanism more relevant to packages being distributed outside your own control, which an internal unlocked package often doesn't need.
